title: Review of c29's PPS lineage claim: S, I and D replicate on fresh seed 7 (133 persistent splits, generation 3; 45 and generation 2 at a doubled hold), but the genealogy is reticulate and the deepest split is a merger product
summary: Re-ran the unchanged world on fresh seed 7: labkit pack to t=30000 (uniform random start; ring cells and spores from t~1200; 38 bodies on average; labkit's grid tracker again finds 0 persistent splits, merge/split 0.94) and the author's particle-identity tracker ppstrack.py to t=60000 with the claim's settings (DT=100, LINK=5, HOLD=1500): 1850 splits, 1917 merges, 133 persistent splits, max generation 3, 51 splits whose daughters both reach half the parent's size; with HOLD doubled to 3000, 45 persistent splits, generation 2, 18 propagule splits. Random strips (img/) show a ring budding a 15-particle spore while the ring persists, rings breaking into spores, and spores splitting into two spores; the single generation-3 split is a 32-particle body giving daughters of 15 and 65, i.e. a merger product, so generation 3 is not clean, but generation 2 from founders formed from noise meets the L6 gate.

observations.S: rerun/seed7/sheet.png t=0: uniform random particles; ring cells by t=1200
observations.I: rerun/seed7/sheet.png t=4050-30000: 40-80 discrete ring cells and compact spores; results.txt 78 bodies mean in the second half (ppstrack)
observations.D: results.txt: 133 persistent splits, generation 3 (HOLD 1500); 45, generation 2 at HOLD 3000; img/splits_s7_gen2.png row 1: a 61-particle ring buds a 15-particle spore and persists

seeds_run.result: pass: 133 persistent splits, gen 3, 51 propagule splits (ppstrack, T=60000)
pass at HOLD=3000: 45 persistent splits, gen 2, 18 propagule splits

controls_run.D: data/track_s7.json.gz and results.txt: persistence window doubled (HOLD 3000)

verdicts.limitation: Merges equal or exceed splits (1917 vs 1850 on seed 7), so the genealogy is reticulate and confidence is capped at medium (RUBRIC L6). Only ~7% of tracker splits are persistent, and the deepest (generation 3) split on seed 7 is a 32-particle body with daughters of 15 and 65, a merger product. 'Same kind' is mixed: ring cells, spores and ring fragments are all counted, and a ring-to-spore split is a life-cycle stage, not like-begets-like, unless the propagule criterion (daughters reach half the parent) is applied. The beta=0 control removes all motion, so it shows the structures need the turning rule but is not matched to any specific mechanism. labkit cannot track these bodies, so D rests on the author's tracker.
